ROLE: Guarantee that at least extra further bytes can be appended without another allocation, growing geometrically, with overflow and allocation failure reported and contents untouched on failure.

VAR.NAME: SIZE_MAX
VAR.ROLE: Upper bound used for overflow detection (stdint.h)

LOGIC.INPUT: buf (NULL allowed) and extra, the number of additional bytes that must become writable above buf->len.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If buf is NULL return -1. 2) If extra > SIZE_MAX - buf->len return -1 (the request cannot be represented; contents unchanged). 3) needed = buf->len + extra; if needed <= buf->cap return 0 (no allocation). 4) Choose newcap = buf->cap ? buf->cap : 64, then double newcap while newcap < needed, but if doubling would overflow (newcap > SIZE_MAX / 2) set newcap = needed and stop, so newcap >= needed always. 5) tmp = realloc(buf->data, newcap); if tmp is NULL return -1 and leave data/len/cap exactly as they were (the old allocation stays owned by the buffer). 6) Store buf->data = tmp and buf->cap = newcap; len is unchanged so the existing contents are preserved. Return 0.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: 0 when buf has capacity for at least len+extra bytes and all previously stored bytes are intact; -1 on overflow or allocation failure with the buffer completely unchanged.
INVARIANTS_USED: len <= cap after every successful call
failed reserve leaves contents and ownership unchanged
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: buf is NULL or a valid buffer; buf->data is either NULL or a live allocation of buf->cap bytes.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: On success cap >= len + extra; on failure the triple (data,len,cap) is bitwise unchanged.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe; the caller owns the buffer exclusively.
